title: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: among locally finite planar configurations of centered disk density one, the triangular lattice minimizes the lower-limit energy E_g for every completely monotone g of squared distance, including infinite energies. The proof builds a sharp Gaussian auxiliary pair for every alpha>0. Theorem 2.1 constructs it for k>=2.36 using cardinal interpolation on the periodic superset 12Z+{0,1,3,4,7,9}, a finite-block/Schur-complement exact interpolation, and Arb-certified Bernstein and tail sign bounds. Fourier complementation covers alpha<1. The result then passes through a Cohn–de Courcy-Ireland density LP and shifted Hausdorff–Bernstein mixtures. A corollary covers Riesz/log renormalized and jellium energies for 0<=s<2.
coverage:
Read Sections 1–7 in full. Section 8 (renormalized/jellium corollary) was only skimmed, and Appendices A/B were not read line by line.

Analytic checks, all of which hold:
- Density LP (Cauchy–Schwarz against the background disk, uniform cross-term error).
- Gaussian duality for alpha<1 (the slack identities give the correct contacts, using A*=JA).
- Positive-mixture transfer: Fatou/Tonelli order, the endpoint v=1 when L(1)=inf, and removing the epsilon shift only in the lattice sum.
- The Gaussian-transform derivation of lambda(t), z(t).
- The cardinal-measure density formula and its folding.
- Lemma 3.1 quadrature error, including the disk bounds, the exponents below 182 and 160, and the Cauchy tail.
- Schur-complement invertibility and the correction estimates.
- The box-lower lemma (concavity in x justifies the vertex minimum).
- Target supports at m=0, 1, 3 (monotonicity in k and the Jensen step).
- The tail argument: the double zeros of Z_i, the second-derivative bound, and the sine barrier.
